title: Will every rectangle in the blackboard ratio look the same?
description: The width and height of a blackboard are written as a ratio and reduced to the simplest form. Rectangles of different sizes with that ratio are drawn and found to have the same shape.
teaching_notes: One idea: rectangles with the same width to height ratio have the same shape, whatever their size. Watch for students who think a bigger rectangle must look different.

video_script.why: The child uses one factor on both sides of a rectangle to draw different sizes of the same shape.
video_script.substitution: Write width to height, reduce it to the simplest form, then multiply both terms by one factor to draw rectangles.
video_script.anchor: a classroom blackboard with its width and height, and a notebook page for the rectangles
video_script.payoff_line: Every rectangle in the ratio three to one has the same shape, though the sizes differ.

final_answer.value: 3 : 1; every rectangle in that ratio has the same shape though sizes differ
final_answer.spoken: three to one; every rectangle in that ratio has the same shape, though the sizes differ

maths_rules: sample blackboard used to show the method (the book asks the child to measure their own board): width 360 cm and height 120 cm, so 360 : 120
rectangles in the ratio 3 : 1: 3 cm by 1 cm; 9 cm by 3 cm (factor 3); 6 cm by 2 cm (factor 2)
check: 360 ÷ 120 = 3; 3 ÷ 1 = 3; 9 ÷ 3 = 3; 6 ÷ 2 = 3; width is 3 times the height each time
video_script.design: One idea: the same ratio gives the same shape at any size. Uses the factor of change from the solved example. The board and the notebook page stay for the whole video.
open_questions: The book asks the child to measure their own blackboard, so the video shows the method on a sample board of 360 cm by 120 cm. These numbers are not in the book.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='simple'/>Divide both terms by their highest common factor. The ratio we get is called its simplest form.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the ratio of width to height, and draw rectangles with that ratio.
<bookmark mark='w'/>Step one, write the width first, which is three hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Then write the height, which is one hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is three hundred sixty to one hundred twenty.

marks.s: 3 : 1 is boxed as the simplest form

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step two, the highest common factor is one hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Three hundred sixty divided by one hundred twenty is three. One hundred twenty divided by itself is one.
<bookmark mark='s'/>The simplest form is three to one.
